speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I see you are experiencing a pruritic rash, fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. To help me understand your condition better, how long have these symptoms been present?

speaker: Patient
text: 11-year-old girl. The patient has been experiencing a mildly pruritic rash on her trunk and extremities for 2 days. One week ago, she developed symptoms of low-grade fever, rhinorrhea, and headache. A facial rash appeared 4 days later, sparing the perioral area.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Erythema Infectiosum (Fifth Disease) caused by Parvovirus B19.

Based on your description of a "slapped cheek" facial rash sparing the perioral area, appearing after a viral prodrome of fever and rhinorrhea, this is the classic presentation of Fifth Disease. I will be monitoring your condition, but please ensure you seek immediate care if you develop severe joint pain or breathing difficulties.
